definitions.gloss: to be extremely busy; to be overwhelmed with work
definitions.explanation: Describes a state of being so busy that one has barely any free time. A formal expression emphasizing the extreme degree of busyness.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{多忙|たぼう}を{極|きわ}めた。
examples.english: The year-end period was extremely busy.

examples.japanese: {新|しん}プロジェクトが{始|はじ}まり、{部署|ぶしょ}{全体|ぜんたい}が{多忙|たぼう}を{極|きわ}めている。
examples.english: A new project started, and the entire department is extremely busy.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}は{海外出張|かいがいしゅっちょう}と{国内|こくない}の{会議|かいぎ}で{多忙|たぼう}を{極|きわ}め、{家族|かぞく}との{時間|じかん}がまったく{取|と}れなかった。
examples.english: The president was overwhelmed with overseas business trips and domestic meetings, unable to find any time for family.

notes:
A formal expression for being extremely busy. {極|きわ}める means "to reach an extreme" or "to exhaust," so the expression literally means "to reach the extreme of busyness."

THE ～を{極|きわ}める PATTERN:
This pattern means "to reach the extreme of" and appears in several set expressions:
- {贅沢|ぜいたく}を{極|きわ}める: to live in extreme luxury
- {混乱|こんらん}を{極|きわ}める: to be in utter chaos
- {困難|こんなん}を{極|きわ}める: to be extremely difficult
- {繁栄|はんえい}を{極|きわ}める: to prosper greatly

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {忙|いそが}しい: busy — everyday adjective
- てんてこ{舞|ま}い: being in a frantic rush — more colloquial and vivid
- {目|め}が{回|まわ}る{忙|いそが}しさ: dizzyingly busy — colloquial
- {超多忙|ちょうたぼう}: super busy — more casual modern expression
